title: New Aoki Infostealer Targets AI Coding Assistant Credentials
key_facts: Symantec's Threat Hunter Team reported on 15 Oct 2026 that new versions of the Aoki infostealer target credential and session files of AI coding assistants
Earlier versions focused on browser, crypto wallet and password manager data

Newest version targeted .claude.json, Claude desktop cookies, ChatGPT cookies and Codex config.toml and .env files, plus tokens for GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Gemini, JetBrains AI Assistant and Kiro, and AWS credentials
Stolen tokens let an attacker act under a developer's identity and usage allowance and may expose repositories, cloud services and CI/CD pipelines
Aoki first seen earlier in 2026; no known threat group or link to existing malware; target list suggests financial motive
quote_evidence: New versions of the Aoki infostealer are targeting credential and session files used by popular AI coding assistants, a new report by Symantec has warned.
Like card data, a stolen AI key can be cashed in directly, either through resale or by running up usage on the victim's account
why_it_matters_hint: Developers' AI-tool logins are now a target for data-stealing malware.
notes: Single security-vendor report (Symantec); read via Infosecurity Magazine. The article's ownership phrase for Cursor is not repeated.
